questions.question: What are arrays and hashes in Ruby?
questions.title: Arrays and Hashes in Ruby
questions.direct_answer: Arrays and Hashes are Ruby's core collections. An Array is an ordered, integer-indexed list: [1, 2, 3]; a[0] == 1; a << 4 appends; a.each, a.map, a[0..1] (slice). A Hash is a key-value map: {name: 'Ada', age: 30}; h[:name] == 'Ada'; h[:city] = 'NYC' adds. Use an Array when you have a list (order matters, duplicates ok, index by position); use a Hash when you map keys to values (lookup by key, unique keys). Both are mutable and include Enumerable (so each, map, select, reduce work on both). Arrays keep insertion order; Hashes also keep insertion order (since 1.9). Choose Array for sequences, Hash for lookups/records.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you know an Array is an ordered indexed list and a Hash is a key-value map, and when to use each.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Using an Array for key-based lookup (O(n) — use a Hash), or a Hash when order/duplicates matter (use an Array).
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Array = ordered, indexed list ([1,2,3]; a[0]; <<). Hash = key-value map ({k:v}; h[:k]). Array for sequences; Hash for lookups. Both mutable + Enumerable.

sections.title: Array vs Hash
sections.content:
Array = ordered indexed list; Hash = key-value map. Array for sequences; Hash for lookups. Both Enumerable.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Array: [1,2,3]] --> I[indexed: a[0]]
  H[Hash: {k:v}] --> K[keyed: h[:k]]
  A --> E[Enumerable: each/map]
  H --> E
```

sections.title: Arrays and hashes
sections.content:
```ruby
# Array: ordered, integer-indexed list
a = [10, 20, 30]
a[0]            # 10 (index by position)
a << 40         # append -> [10, 20, 30, 40]
a.length        # 4
a.each { |x| puts x }
a.map  { |x| x * 2 }   # [20, 40, 60, 80]
a[1..2]         # [20, 30] (slice, inclusive)
a.include?(20) # true

# Hash: key-value map
h = { name: 'Ada', age: 30 }
h[:name]        # 'Ada' (lookup by key)
h[:age] = 31    # set
h[:city] = 'NYC'# add a key
h.keys          # [:name, :age, :city]
h.each { |k, v| puts "#{k}=#{v}" }
h.delete(:age)  # remove a key

# Both are MUTABLE and Enumerable (each/map/select/reduce work on both).
# Array: order + duplicates ok, index by position. Use for SEQUENCES.
# Hash: unique keys, lookup by key. Use for LOOKUPS / records.
# Both keep insertion order (Hash since 1.9).
```

sections.title: Common Mistakes
items: Using an Array for key-based lookup (O(n) — use a Hash for O(1)).
A Hash when order or duplicates matter (use an Array).
String vs symbol keys mixed up (h['name'] vs h[:name] — different keys).

sections.title: Key Takeaways
items: An Array is an ordered, integer-indexed list ([1,2,3]; a[0]; <<).
A Hash is a key-value map ({name: 'Ada'}; h[:name]; h[:k]=v).
Use an Array for sequences (order/duplicates ok); a Hash for lookups (unique keys).
Both are mutable and include Enumerable (each/map/select/reduce work on both).
Arrays keep insertion order; Hashes also keep insertion order since Ruby 1.9.
